claims.text: Combining AIMD with machine-learning regression enables prediction of melting temperature across high-entropy alloys.
The combined AIMD-ML approach can predict enthalpy and entropy of fusion across high-entropy alloys.
The combined AIMD-ML approach can predict volume change at melting across high-entropy alloys.
The combined AIMD-ML approach can predict liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across high-entropy alloys.
AIMD-generated thermodynamic data near melting can be used to train models that interpolate properties across HEA compositional space.
Controlled temperature ramps, periodic boundary conditions, and converged DFT parameters are appropriate simulation conditions for the proposed approach.
Local atomic configurations and short-range order govern phase stability during melting.
Local atomic configurations and short-range order affect the energy landscape during melting.
AIMD captures atomic dynamics and thermodynamic fluctuations near the melting point.
Machine-learning interpolation reduces the computational cost of predictions across high-dimensional compositional space.
The two-tier approach combines first-principles accuracy with the efficiency of data-driven interpolation.
The integrated approach is expected to predict melting temperatures within approximately ±5% of experimental values.
The integrated approach is expected to predict fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and volume change at melting with accuracy comparable to its approximately ±5% melting-temperature accuracy.
The integrated approach is expected to capture trends in liquid-phase thermodynamic properties accurately.
Conventional experimental calorimetry is slower than the proposed computational approach.
Standalone DFT is less transferable across composition space because of its high computational cost.
Accuracy may decline for compositions with extreme configurational disorder or compositions far outside the ML training distribution.
Typical AIMD cell sizes may fail to capture relevant long-range interactions.
ML performance depends on the breadth and quality of the training dataset.
